title: ChemPrint deep learning nominates AXL and BRD4 inhibitors with a 46% in vitro hit rate
summary: The ChemPrint molecular-geometric deep learning model, trained with t-SNE data splitting, reached average AUROC 0.897 for AXL and 0.876 for BRD4 retrospectively. In a zero-shot prospective in vitro study, 19 of 41 nominated compounds inhibited AXL or BRD4 at 20 uM or below (46% hit rate), with average maximum Tanimoto similarity 0.36 to the training set. The model belongs to a company platform and hits are micromolar. Preprint of 2024-03-27.
ai_technology: ChemPrint molecular-geometric deep learning model within the GALILEO platform for compound nomination

evidence.tested: Zero-shot prospective in vitro testing of 41 nominated compounds against AXL and BRD4.
evidence.unknown: Potency optimization, selectivity and peer-reviewed status are not established; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A deep learning model nominated candidate inhibitors that were then tested in vitro.
